title: Node.js fs/promises, Buffer, and path differences
hook: Node extends JavaScript with Buffer for binary data and fs/promises for async file I/O — the building blocks for reading SQS payload files, writing prerender cache, and handling Redis protocol bytes without blocking the event loop.

blocks.text: **fs.promises**: Promise-based readFile, writeFile, mkdir, readdir — non-blocking libuv thread pool for I/O. **Buffer**: Uint8Array subclass for binary; **alloc**, **from**, **toString(encoding)**. **path.join**, **path.resolve**: OS-correct separators. **file:// URLs**: `import.meta.url` for ESM path resolution.

readFileSync in request handler blocks event loop. Buffer vs string for Redis payloads avoids UTF-8 corruption on binary. Wrong path.join on Windows breaks deploy. Large files: createReadStream not readFile.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: readFileSync in HTTP handler. String encoding on binary. path concatenation with + instead of join.

blocks.text: fs.open with FileHandle for concurrent reads. UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE for heavy fs. Prerender writes static HTML to dist/ — fs at build time OK sync; runtime must be async.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: readFileSync in Express route. Confuses Buffer with string. No path.join on Windows paths.

interviewTakeaways: fs.promises async — no event loop block.
Buffer for binary; UTF-8 string for text JSON.
60s: readFileSync blocks loop. fs.promises + await. Buffer for Redis binary. path.join ESM __dirname via import.meta.url. Stream large files.
commonPitfalls: Weak: sync fs in server hot path.
Weak: redis.get string for PNG bytes.
Strong: promises + Buffer + atomic write + stream large.
